summary: This diff adds two new standalone scripts (auto_phase_continuation.py, tight_task_validation.py), wires the latter into task-gateway.py's cmd_start as an additional pre-dispatch gate, and records/approves one new crontab entry per the project's established OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED + CRONTAB_APPROVED_SNAPSHOT convention (matching prior entries in the same file, no .github/workflows/** touched). The code is additive, uses list-form subprocess calls throughout (no shell=True, no command injection), does not touch migrations/schema/auth/payment/security paths, and is consistent with the tier1 classification. The design is notably careful about not trusting self-reported phase status (cross-checks via gh pr list --state merged, with a documented master-branch fallback for the closed-PR/recovery-commit case), and the new tight_task_validation.py gate is a faithful, narrowly-scoped port that explicitly does not retroactively block legacy free-text prompts. That said, this introduces a real, unsupervised, every-30-minutes automation that dispatches live tasks/PRs with no default rate limit (the crontab entry passes no --limit, so every ready phase across every initiative dispatches in one run) and its de-duplication relies on a fuzzy keyword+phase-number heuristic against task titles/PR names rather than explicit persisted state linking a phase to its dispatched task — a heuristic miss could cause the same phase to be re-dispatched on repeated cron ticks. dispatch() also writes generated prompts to a predictable /tmp path via plain open(path, 'w') with no cleanup, which is a minor hardening gap on a shared host. None of these rise to a blocking defect for an additive tier1 change, but they warrant close monitoring of the first several real cron runs.
issues: already_dispatched()'s dedup is a fuzzy phase-number+keyword match against task-gateway/gh pr titles, not explicit persisted state (no 'phase X -> dispatched task Y' record) -- a heuristic miss could cause the same phase to be re-dispatched every 30 minutes indefinitely.

The crontab entry invokes auto_phase_continuation.py with no --limit, so a single run can dispatch every ready phase across every initiative simultaneously with no default throttle, despite the project's own stated 2-3 concurrent-worker capacity guidance.

dispatch() writes generated prompts to a predictable path in /tmp (/tmp/auto_phase_continuation_{title}.txt) via plain open(path, 'w') with no O_EXCL/tempfile usage and never cleans the file up afterward -- a minor symlink/race and disk-litter concern on a shared multi-user host.

The new OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED entry is self-authored and self-approved by the same task that added the cron entry, citing its own dispatched SPEC as the approval basis -- consistent with prior entries in this same file, so not a new pattern, but worth periodic Owner spot-checking given it recurs on every cron addition.
